gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, for a US iPhone owner, Apple does not let non-Apple wearables send text replies. Apple's ANCS Bluetooth service gives accessories only a generic 'positive' or 'negative' action per notification. Apple's newer AccessoryNotifications framework does support quick replies, but it works only on iPhones in the EU signed in with an EU Apple Account. As a result, Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Inspire 3 and Garmin vívoactive 6 replies are Android-only, Apple Watch is the only native reply-from-wrist option on iPhone, and Amazfit gets around the block only through a third-party Beeper bridge.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages and the top results. The cited Apple Support Series 11 tech specs (support.apple.com/en-mide/125093) state only that the watch needs iPhone 11 or later with iOS 26. They say nothing about what other watches can do on iPhone. The body of the cited Google Store Charge 6 specs page would not render, so I could not check its text. apple.com/watch/compare mentions iPhone requirements for features but not third-party limits. Among uncited results, sekin.in says Charge 6 has 'documented preset quick replies' with an Android phone, so part of this is already out there. It does not say iPhone blocks replies, does not explain why, does not cover Garmin or Amazfit, and does not mention the EU-only Apple framework. ChatGPT's answer listed 'Calls, messages' as smartwatch traits and asked which phone the shopper uses, but never said that the phone decides whether a tracker can reply at all.
decides: The phone question becomes the first fork. On Android: Apple Watch is out because it pairs only with iPhone. Fitbit and Garmin can reply with quick replies, but on Charge 6 and Inspire 3 there is no wrist payment on iPhone either way. On iPhone in the US: the cheapest way to reply from the wrist natively is the Apple Watch SE 3. Amazfit Active 2 and Bip 6 can reply only after setting up Zepp Messenger with a Beeper account. Fitbit and Garmin buyers on iPhone get read-only notifications. Our current table already shows 'no replies on iPhone' for Charge 6 and 'replies on Android only' for vívoactive 6. This finding gives the reason, extends it to Inspire 3, and should change the Amazfit cells to 'replies on iPhone via Zepp Messenger + Beeper'.

findings.label: What a non-Apple accessory can do with an iPhone notification over ANCS
findings.value: Only a 'positive' or 'negative' action, chosen by iOS (for example, answer or decline a call). The spec defines no text-reply action.
findings.note: Quotes: 'EventFlagPositiveAction: A positive action exists…', 'EventFlagNegativeAction…', and 'performing a positive action on an Incoming Call notification may answer it, while performing a negative action may decline it.' The appendix with ActionID values did not render, but the body describes only these two generic actions.

findings.label: Apple's quick-reply framework for third-party accessories: availability
findings.value: iOS 26.5 or later. Works for customers only on iPhones located in the EU and signed in with an EU Apple Account.
findings.note: Quote: 'Customer installations of your app can only use the framework on devices located in the EU that are signed in with an Apple Account with an EU country or region.' The framework does support 'typing text in a quick reply'. So a US iPhone owner cannot use it.

findings.label: Phone requirement
findings.value: iPhone 11 or later (including iPhone SE 2nd gen or later) with iOS 26 or later. Android is not listed.
findings.source_title: Apple Watch Series 11 - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: The same page says 'Apple Watch Ultra 3, Apple Watch Series 11, and Apple Watch SE 3 require iPhone 11 or later with iOS 26 or later.' This is the regional (en-mide) page that ChatGPT cited. Battery on the same page: up to 24 h normal use, 38 h in Low Power Mode.
